$comment: What the agents actually cost. Every Agent dispatch returns tokens, tool calls and wall-clock duration; until 2026-09-03 those were read once in a notification and discarded, so the repository could say what its agents FOUND and not what they COST. This ledger is the record. It is append-only and hand-entered from each dispatch's own returned usage block — there is no API to collect it from, which is stated rather than pretended otherwise.
the_rule: One row per dispatch, entered when the dispatch returns. `outcome` records what the run DID, not whether it succeeded — a refusal that caught a real defect is a successful run of an attestation and must not read as a failure. Cost without outcome is a number nobody can act on.

completeness.$comment: Honest scope, because a cost ledger that looks complete and is not would misprice every future decision made from it.
completeness.known_incomplete: Dispatches before 2026-09-01 are NOT recorded — their usage blocks were consumed in conversation and are unrecoverable. Several 2026-09-01/02 runs are also missing: only rows whose exact usage block could be quoted are entered, and a run recalled but not quoted was left out rather than estimated. Totals below are therefore a FLOOR, not a measurement.
completeness.not_captured: Main-session cost is not here at all. Only subagent dispatches return a usage block; the orchestrating session's own tokens are invisible to it. The true cost of this work is higher than any total this file can produce, by an unknown margin.

Found an arithmetic defect in the SOURCE that reached the stakeholder document: Phase 3 reports 275 confidence cells against a grid it describes as 55x6=330; 275 is exactly 55x5, a five-column total. runs.task: Render the competitor coverage board (ART-013)
runs.found: Refused the brief's encoding. The dispatch said 'status - evidence tier'; the dataviz job table names TIER as the Ordinal job in the row directly above Status, which is a reserved good->critical scale. The instruction would have put 'never profiled' on the same axis as 'critical' - reading as a verdict on those competitors rather than a gap in our study, the exact misreading D-001 exists to prevent. Built a validated one-hue ordinal ramp instead and gave the three-way coverage split NO hue at all, shape and word only. Same class it caught in ART-010 (outcome cannot wear status colour) - second time it has refused a colour job from its brief. Also surfaced that D-001's text says 6 never-profiled where ART-011 reconciles to 8, and followed the 8/2/6 split with the discrepancy stated rather than silently resolved.

runs.task: Benchmark best-in-class interactive research dashboards
runs.found: Contradicted ART-013's central choice with empirical work. Song & Szafir (IEEE VIS 2018): encodings that HIGHLIGHT missing data score higher on perceived quality than ones that DOWNPLAY it (alpha-blend, hatching, dashed), and removal scores lowest of all. ART-013's hatched grey blanks are the downplay condition, which tested badly on exactly the credibility axis D-001 exists to protect. Also: typed-absence vocabularies (StatCan 5 symbols, MDN true/false/null, caniuse grey-? vs red-X); VSUP (Correll/Moritz/Heer CHI 2018) as the right primitive for a value x uncertainty matrix; the Tableau census (n=25,620) placing this in the MAGAZINE genre, median 8 blocks. Debunked four pieces of folklore incl. the '85% ignore interactives' claim, which its own author has publicly corrected.

runs.task: Rebuild the coverage board as v2 (ART-014)
runs.found: CORRECTED THE PAPER THE REDESIGN RESTED ON. Fetched Song & Szafir (IEEE VIS 2018) and checked the brief's three strongest claims against the actual tables: alpha-blending, a DOWNPLAY technique, scored consistently HIGH on perceived quality; removal did NOT score lowest of every condition (Data Absent 4.19 beat the annotation condition's 4.06); and the accuracy loss was Dashed Outline Bars at 75.35% against Data Absent's 76.37%, which was HIGHER. Direction holds, stated strength did not. Also correctly refused to build the 330-cell matrix: neither it nor a 10-cluster x 6 grid exists at cell resolution in ART-012, so it built the two bivariates the evidence does support (48-cell journey, 6-cell load-bearing row) and named the limit. Caught a class collision right-aligning the KPI numerals via a headless render before delivery.

runs.task: Attack the v2 coverage board (ART-014)
runs.found: 3 blockers, all reproduced independently by the main session. DC-01: the mid-page objects silently re-base from 14 competitors to 6 — the cluster chart is denominated on 330 (55x6) not 770 (55x14), so its WORST bar reads 66.7% four inches below the board's own 24.5% KPI; recomputed on 770 the complement is 581/770 = 75.5%, exact. The journey grid draws 48 of the 112 cells its own KPI counts. DC-02: the VSUP is broken — value and uncertainty ramps are INTERLEAVED by luminance (teal.90 Y=0.0195 sits between gap.90 and gap.80; teal.70 0.0862 vs gap.70 0.0846), so suppressing for uncertainty moves a cell DOWN the value scale. DC-03: 3 @media print blocks and 0 print-color-adjust, so printed the eight render as white text on blank rows while validation.md asserts print carries everything. Also caught assumption A-4 asserting an uncleared Gate A on tokens that tokens.json records as APPROVED by the user on 2026-09-02.

runs.task: Audit the v2 coverage board for accessibility (ART-015)
runs.found: 46 checks, 11 findings (2 error, 5 warning, 4 info), 7 explicitly UNCHECKED. Independently reproduced the two headline claims to two decimals (warmGray.80 on bone 9.79:1; white on it 11.57:1) rather than accepting them. F-01: .gapnote carries opacity 0.86, which fades the whole element -- stripe background AND white text together -- toward the page ground, resolving to 3.85:1 against the lighter half of the stripe; it documented getting the compositing wrong on a first pass and redoing it. F-08 (error): six <details> controls have a literally EMPTY <summary> with the entire label in CSS ::before content -- an unlabelled control for assistive tech, and also the exact mechanism design-critic had hypothesised for the word-count discrepancy. F-04 hit the SAME VSUP collision design-critic found (1.30:1 vs 1.305:1) by a different route, neither agent having seen the other run.

runs.task: Build v3 of the coverage board (ART-016)
runs.found: All 3 blockers and all 11 a11y findings resolved; 18 of 21 critique findings fixed, 2 kept as documented judgment calls, 1 knowingly left with reasons. Traced Blocker 2 deeper than the brief did: tokens.json is a Carbon mirror where EVERY hue family shares one universal lightness ladder, so any two ordinal ramps at matching step numbers are luminance-identical regardless of hue -- there is no non-colliding third ramp on this token set. Fix moves confidence off colour entirely onto a dashed border and draws absence hollow so it is never a competing fill. Also found tokens.json disagrees with ITSELF on Gate A (C-035), correcting both design-critic and the main session, who had each read only the batch note. Caught four of its own off-token literals before delivery.

runs.task: Benchmark navigation, disclosure and graphical craft with colour frozen
runs.found: Answered the central question -- where graphical richness comes from when colour is spent. Bertin: value and TEXTURE are ordered variables, so the palette freeze does not lock shape or texture. Top move is unit/dot-matrix encoding: isotype practice makes an unfilled unit communicate absence STRUCTURALLY, so the 8 blanks become a hole in the pattern rather than a different colour. Sharp corollary: with a luminance-matched ramp a legend is ACTIVELY HARDER to decode than direct labels, so direct labelling is not a preference here but a fix. Bateman CHI 2010: embellishment does not help comprehension but significantly helps RECALL at 2-3 weeks -- which is this board's actual job. Killed two more pieces of folklore: the '5-7 KPIs max' rule attributed to NN/g appears nowhere in their publications and is Miller's 7+/-2 transplanted by SEO blogs, and the 'dashboards become wallpaper in two weeks' claim has no traceable data. Ruled OUT scrollytelling: every case study found is narrative journalism, not a reference tool three audiences jump around in. Two Opus dispatches died on 529 before this one ran on Sonnet.

runs.task: Freeze the foundations baseline and verify the lightness-ladder property
runs.found: Baseline frozen: 829 leaves, canonical-JSON sha256 1926c393... (survives reformatting). VERIFIED the universal lightness ladder rather than taking it on trust -- worst-case pairwise contrast between any two hue families at the same step, all 12 families, is 1.055:1. Then went past the brief and checked the REGISTERED palette against it, finding C-036: cf-chart-palette's four primary series sit at under 0.4% luminance separation, so the system's only sanctioned chart palette cannot distinguish its own categories. Also found 731 of 829 tokens (88%) are referenced by nothing in the component index, including 100% of semantic-dark, motion, elevation and density, and that the five-axis framing in CLAUDE.md omits density -- tokens.json has 8 top-level keys, a reconciliation that existed nowhere in the repo. Changed no token value.

runs.task: Write four component-specs (ART-017 to ART-020) — first exercise of the membrane
runs.found: Four specs delivered with a verify-contrast.py beside each that re-resolves every alias, recomputes every ratio, validates against component.schema.json and FAILS if the name already appears in the index -- it caught one of its own transposed figures before delivery. Found C-037 (Gate B's component detector is PascalCase-only, so the first prohibition has never been tested on any artifact this repo ships) and C-038 (the Carbon adapter deletes any authored L2 entry, making the RED exit condition unreachable). Corrected the MAGNITUDE of C-036 four minutes after token-keeper filed it: 0 of 108 adjacent-step pairs clear 2:1, so a single-hue ordinal ramp on bone supports at most TWO mutually-3:1 steps. Measured semantic.focus on teal.60 at 1.003:1 -- the focus ring vanishes on the lightest fill, no token substitution fixes it, hence a two-tone ring. Also: cf-badge's four kinds sit within 0.025 of each other and its kind axis is hue-only, failing 1.4.1. Diffed the audit by (severity, check, message) rather than totals and REFUSED to claim a delta that token-keeper had written concurrently four minutes earlier.

runs.task: Benchmark how mature design systems govern data visualization
runs.found: One-sided across every system checked. USWDS states it outright: 'The data visualizations components are guidance-only and do not include any Component Code.' Spectrum, Polaris and Carbon ship separate packages; Primer and GOV.UK ship guidance with no code. None folds chart internals into component registration. Resolved the blurry line with a rule two systems reached independently: chart anatomy is whatever the chart's own rendering logic draws (marks, legend, tooltip, axis); a separate DOM element a human clicks or reads as a number (KPI tile, filter) is an ordinary UI component. Carbon confirms directly -- Tile is a plain UI component, not in @carbon/charts. Counter-case argued properly and it does NOT support folding charts into the index: the documented failure is DRIFT nobody catches because no one inspects the assembled screen, whose answer is adversarial real-screen validation. Verified by direct fetch that NNG publishes no '5-7 KPIs' guidance anywhere -- the attribution is false. Supplied a usable numeric contract from Primer: 3:1 marks, 4.5:1 axis text, first line solid with stroke-style differentiation without colour.

runs.task: Build v4 of the coverage board (ART-021) — unit charts, nav, disclosure
runs.found: Rebuilt as an actual dashboard: 770-cell and 112-cell isotype unit charts where absence is drawn as a hole, a sticky nav rail with scrollspy and deep links, and 155 click-to-pin provenance triggers into a side panel. Every legend removed -- direct labels only. Prose cut 2183->1460 visible words (33%), 4058->2142 all-DOM (47%). THE FINDING: the <details>-forced-open-under-print CSS technique that v2 AND v3 both shipped does not actually reveal hidden content in this Chrome build -- proved with a real --print-to-pdf render plus PyMuPDF text extraction, then fixed with beforeprint/afterprint toggling the real open attribute. So v3's print claim, which the main session reported to the user as resolving DC-03, was unverified in exactly the way DC-03 warned about. Also corrected the brief: ADR-021 was still PROPOSED when the dispatch opened it and flipped to ACCEPTED mid-run; it confirmed this rather than assuming. Caught five defects in its own build before delivery, including all 155 triggers missing a default aria-expanded.

runs.task: Plain-language copy deck for the coverage board (ART-022)
runs.found: Delivered a copy deck: 65-word standfirst, inline definitions indexed to first use, quote-current/replace-with pairs for every caption, and a concrete relocation plan for the 46 reference codes. Confirmed the predicted gap honestly rather than papering over it: ART-011/012 establish that Luma is 'a first-time-traveller travel product at ideation' but NOT what it sells — and it identified that the 'referral layer' in ART-012 is the study's own UNADOPTED recommendation with no acceptance recorded anywhere, so using it as a product description would have asserted a decision nobody made. Found C-039 while reading, outside its brief: five rownotes truncated mid-sentence with the full text present in the same file. Also flagged that its own direct/adjacent/analogous definition is INFERRED from the roster rather than quoted, because the citation for it points into research/sources/, which it was forbidden to open.

runs.task: Build v5 with the plain-language deck applied (ART-023)
runs.found: Fixed C-039 — all five truncated rownotes restored verbatim from the panel JSON — and, finding no generator to patch at source, shipped verify-rownotes.py which passes on v5 and reproduces all five defects when pointed at v4. Applied the copy deck: standfirst with the 'what Luma sells' gap left visible, seven jargon groups defined at first use, direct/adjacent/analogous marked Inferred on the page. Re-verified every do-not-regress invariant against the live payload rather than asserting them, including a fresh --print-to-pdf extraction and all six CDP interaction tests. TWO CLAIMS THE MAIN SESSION COULD NOT REPRODUCE: it reported reference codes in prose falling 18->2; measured the same way on both versions, mid-sentence codes in the default-visible flow went 32->25, and total visible codes ROSE 46->58 because provenance was relocated rather than removed. And words rose 2131->3463 (+62%), which it states as expected, but the hero moved from 62 words down the page to 243 — the entry point the v4 benchmark was built around.

runs.task: Write the locked 14-competitor capture research plan (ART-024)
runs.found: First dispatch of this agent. Seven corrections to its brief. (1) Only FOUR competitors are net-new, not seven — Airbnb, Tripadvisor and Rentalcars are already in the client's own standing set, and burying four real additions among seven weakens the argument that must survive. (2) Loyalty is NOT a ninth stage — it occurs inside other stages, and a ninth stage would discard the in-line occurrences where business goal 8's answer lives. (3) A capture may never become a ledger record — CLAUDE.md forbids minting a ledger ID for a measurement — with the sharp corollary that transcribing a user review from a competitor site would create an unresolvable user quote and breach prohibition 2. (4) The main session's 'write captures to a file immediately' advice DOUBLES cost rather than reducing it: context already spent is re-emitted as tool input; the real levers are the screenshot never entering context and the a11y tree going to disk unread. Revised to ~198k per competitor and 16-20 sessions, not 14. (5) Stage list crossed with state list yields 120 screens against a 40-70 budget. (6) The scenario names FIVE user types and SKILL.md names one — an undeclared disagreement that is the likely origin of the prior round's single-persona lens. (7) ADR-017 does not exist at the path given. Also found an airport-services roster gap: business goal 5 has no comparator among the fourteen. Self-reported a clean-room breach (C-040).
